criteria.text: Recognizes the dissociation between the two treatments' phenotypes in Api5 OE acini: Akt-branch inhibition reverses the volume, surface-area, cell-number, sphericity and Ki-67 changes but leaves lumen filling and the Laminin V, GM130 and E-cadherin defects in place, whereas MEK/ERK inhibition reverses the size and proliferation changes and in addition restores hollow lumens and all three polarity markers.

grounding.quote: However, inhibition of Akt signalling in Api5 OE spheroids had no effect on polarity (Figure 4j-m).

criteria.text: Uses that dissociation to conclude that the Akt and MEK/ERK branches run in parallel below FGFR1 rather than one through the other - if the Akt branch drove ERK activation, blocking it would also have removed the late lumen-filling and polarity phenotypes - and therefore that blocking one branch leaves the other branch's phosphorylation unchanged.

grounding.quote: To check if there was crosstalk between Akt and ERK signalling pathways, pERK1&2 activation upon Akti addition and pAkt T308 levels upon UO126 addition were investigated (Figure S4j-m). No observable changes were detected, thereby indicating the absence of any crosstalk between the two signalling cascades.

criteria.text: Recognizes that neither single-branch inhibitor changed Api5 or FGF2 levels, so the FGF2/FGFR1/FRS2alpha input feeding both branches is the same as in untreated Api5 OE spheroids.

grounding.quote: Moreover, Api5 and FGF2 levels remained unchanged following ERK inhibition (Figure 5a-c).

criteria.text: Uses the unchanged upstream input to exclude a rebound rise in the untouched branch, concluding specifically that pAkt T308 after MEK/ERK inhibition is unchanged rather than increased by relief of ERK-dependent negative feedback.

grounding.text: Blocking a kinase branch below a receptor does not alter that receptor's own activation when ligand and receptor levels are unchanged; a feedback-driven rise in a parallel branch requires the blocked branch to act back on the shared upstream node.

criteria.text: Justifies the two same-branch readouts as on-target engagement controls - each inhibitor acting at its own node lowers its own downstream phosphorylation - consistent with the phenotype reversion each treatment produced in Api5 OE spheroids.

grounding.quote: A decrease in pERK1&2 activation was observed upon UO126 addition in both day 12 and 16 Api5 OE spheroids compared to untreated (Figure S4f, g).
